findings.section: gp3 lets you buy IOPS and throughput without buying more storage
findings.quote: A small database needs many IOPS but little space. gp2 ties IOPS to space, and gp3 does not. ... You raise IOPS and throughput [independently of volume size](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-gp3-performance-independent-of-size), up to [80,000](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-gp3-max-iops-80000) IOPS.
findings.type: technical: condition dropped from a fact
findings.evidence: ebs-gp3-max-iops-80000 (verified): 'You can provision additional IOPS (up to a maximum of 80,000) for an additional cost at a ratio of 500 IOPS per GiB of volume size. Maximum IOPS can be provisioned for volumes 160 GiB or larger (500 IOPS per GiB x 160 GiB = 80,000 IOPS).' Scope of ebs-gp3-performance-independent-of-size: 'within the gp3 IOPS-per-GiB ratio'. gp3 does tie maximum IOPS to size. The chapter's own task ebs-t02 step 6 says 'gp3 allows 500 IOPS per GiB, so 8 GiB allows 4,000 IOPS', which contradicts 'gp3 does not'. A reader who takes the gist believes a 20 GiB gp3 volume can get 80,000 IOPS. Same simplification in 1-fast.md 'Choose it or not' (IOPS and throughput set independently of volume size) and speak ebs-s02 kp2. Fix: add the 500 IOPS per GiB ratio (fact display '500 IOPS per GiB', '160 GiB or larger') once in 2-deep and the A-list row.
findings.resolution: fix-22: 2-deep gp3 intro no longer says gp3 does not tie IOPS to space; step 2 links 500 IOPS per GiB and 160 GiB or larger (ebs-gp3-max-iops-80000); 1-fast choose table and the A-list row add the ratio; speak ebs-s02 kp2 and its 60-second line add the ratio.

findings.section: ebs-s04 follow_ups[1] (4-say.md Prompt 4)
findings.quote: After we turn it on, can someone still create an unencrypted volume? -- Not per volume. Once encryption by default is enabled for a Region, you cannot disable it for individual volumes or snapshots in that Region.
findings.type: technical: unsafe or misleading security answer
findings.evidence: source docs/ebs/latest/userguide/encryption-by-default (fetched 2026-10-09), line 77: '**To disable encryption by default** Use the [disable-ebs-encryption-by-default](...) command.' The Region setting itself can be turned off by anyone allowed ec2:DisableEbsEncryptionByDefault (action listed in iam-userguide, 'Actions for action last accessed information'), after which new volumes can be unencrypted. The prompt is an auditor asking 'how do we stop this from happening again'; 'Not per volume' tells the customer that nobody can create an unencrypted volume, which is false. The answer must say: yes, if someone turns the Region setting off, so restrict ec2:DisableEbsEncryptionByDefault (and check with the Look task). Related wording without the caveat: 2-deep.md FAQ 7 and ebs-t01 step 1 expect ('every new volume that you create in this Region is encrypted') are true only while the setting stays on (note level).
findings.resolution: fix-22: follow-up reworded to 'can someone opt out for one new volume in that Region?', answer grounded in ebs-encryption-by-default-region-setting, no claim that nobody can create an unencrypted volume. The caveat that the Region setting itself can be turned off is not stated: no verified fact; fact request fr-0077 filed.

findings.section: Instance store data lives on the host and ends with the instance
findings.quote: Why does a stop erase it? A started instance is usually [moved to a new host computer](../facts/ec2.md#ec2-stop-start-moves-host-loses-instance-store). So the data is **ephemeral**
findings.type: claims: link does not support the sentence (wrong causal reason)
findings.evidence: instance-store-data-persists-reboot-not-stop: 'When the instance is stopped, hibernated, or terminated, every block of the instance store volume is cryptographically erased.' ec2-stop-start-moves-host-loses-instance-store: 'the instance is moved to a new host computer (though in some cases, it remains on the current host)'. The data is erased at the stop itself, also when the instance stays on the same host; the move is not the reason. Give the cryptographic erase as the reason (the fact is already used in 5-quiz Question 8).
findings.resolution: fix-22: reason is now the cryptographic erase at stop, hibernate or terminate (instance-store-data-persists-reboot-not-stop); the ec2 host-move link is gone.

findings.section: A restored volume can start in any zone but reads slowly at first (step 3, Go deeper, Stop and answer)
findings.quote: With fast snapshot restore, a volume is [fully initialized at creation] ... A full bucket creates [up to 10 initialized volumes] together. ... Ten test volumes come from one snapshot every morning ... What are two fixes? -- Fast snapshot restore on that snapshot in that zone, or an initialization rate.
findings.type: technical: condition dropped from a fact
findings.evidence: ebs-fsr-credit-example-128-gib scope: 'bucket size is MAX (1, MIN (10, 1024 / snapshot size in GiB))' and quote 'if you enable fast snapshot restore for a snapshot with a size of 128 GiB, the fill rate is 0.1333 credits per minute' (8 credits). ebs-fsr-credit-bucket-per-snapshot-az scope: 'with less than one credit, the volume is created without the benefit'; ebs-faq-fsr-up-to-10-volumes: 'Volume creations beyond the limit will proceed as if FSR is not enabled on the snapshot.' Ten volumes at once get FSR only if the snapshot is at most about 102 GiB; the snapshot size is not given, so the answer can be wrong. Either give the snapshot size (5-quiz Question 12 does: 50 GiB, four volumes) or state that the bucket size depends on the snapshot size. Source docs/ebs/latest/userguide/initalize-volume also says the initialization rate is 'especially useful when you are creating multiple volumes simultaneously'.
findings.resolution: fix-22: the FSR Go deeper block was cut (word budget). The Stop-and-answer now names a 20 GiB snapshot, so a full bucket covers up to 10 volumes, and adds dd or fio as the low-cost fix.

findings.section: Copying or sharing a snapshot puts the backup in another Region or account (table)
findings.quote: | Unencrypted | Yes | Yes, unless block public access is on | / | Encrypted, customer managed key | Yes, with the key | No | / | Encrypted, **AWS managed key** | No | No |
findings.type: claims: table rows without fact links
findings.evidence: Hard can/cannot claims in a table with no fact link (RULINGS hard rule 1). Verified facts exist and should be linked: ebs-snapshot-only-unencrypted-public ('You can share only unencrypted snapshots publicly.' / 'Public snapshots of encrypted volumes are not supported, but you can share an encrypted snapshot with specific accounts.'), ebs-snapshot-bpa-blocks-public-sharing-in-region ('any attempt to publicly share snapshots in that Region is automatically blocked'), ebs-snapshot-aws-managed-key-not-shareable, ebs-snapshot-share-encrypted-share-cmk-too. The rows themselves are correct.
findings.resolution: fix-22: table cells link ebs-snapshot-bpa-blocks-public-sharing-in-region, ebs-snapshot-share-encrypted-share-cmk-too, ebs-snapshot-only-unencrypted-public and ebs-snapshot-aws-managed-key-not-shareable.

findings.section: Copying or sharing a snapshot puts the backup in another Region or account (Exam trap)
findings.quote: Many think that any encrypted snapshot can go to a partner account. Only snapshots [encrypted with a customer managed key](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-aws-managed-key-not-shareable) can be shared.
findings.type: claims: universal claim broader than the fact
findings.evidence: As written, the second sentence says no other snapshot can be shared, which contradicts the table row 'Unencrypted | Yes | Yes' a few lines above and ebs-snapshot-share-public-or-specific-accounts ('You can share snapshots publicly with all other AWS accounts, or ... privately with individual AWS accounts'). The fact ebs-snapshot-aws-managed-key-not-shareable is scoped to 'encrypted EBS snapshots'. Fix: 'Of the encrypted snapshots, only those encrypted with a customer managed key can be shared.'
findings.resolution: fix-22: 'Of the encrypted snapshots, only those encrypted with a customer managed key can be shared.'

findings.section: Question 12 (ebs-q018) Why and Why not
findings.quote: until each block has been read once ... Each block is [downloaded from Amazon S3 to the new volume] on first read ... The blocks of an io2 volume are also [downloaded from Amazon S3 to the new volume] on first read
findings.type: claims: explanation says more than the linked fact
findings.evidence: The linked fact ebs-volume-initialization-from-snapshot says only 'For volumes created from snapshots, the data blocks must be downloaded from Amazon S3 to the new volume.' The saved page docs/ebs/latest/userguide/initalize-volume says 'Full volume performance is achieved only once all storage blocks have been downloaded and written to the volume' and 'The default volume initialization rate fluctuates throughout the initialization process': initialization proceeds in the background, not only 'on first read' or 'until each block has been read once'. Remove 'on first read' and 'read once' (the key stays right). Explanation edit only; the stem, options and key do not change.
findings.resolution: fix-22: the explanation cannot be edited without resetting verification, so ebs-q018 is no longer shipped (status verified) and verified ebs-q015 (Multi-Attach, extended) ships in its place; the unsupported 'on first read' text is no longer in the book.

findings.section: ebs-t03 cleanup[0] (after step 7, which has no wait)
findings.quote: "text": "Delete the restored volume.", "command": "aws ec2 delete-volume --volume-id $NEW_ID"
findings.type: technical: cleanup can fail silently
findings.evidence: source docs/cli/latest/reference/ec2/delete-volume line 34: 'Deletes the specified EBS volume. The volume must be in the available state (not attached to an instance).' Step 7 creates NEW_ID from a snapshot and no step waits for it (steps 3 and 4 wait for VOL_ID only). A reader who moves fast deletes a volume that is still `creating`, gets an error, and this cleanup step, unlike ebs-t02's, gives no 'wait and run again' advice; the verify text only says to rerun the verify, which deletes nothing. Add `aws ec2 wait volume-available --volume-ids $NEW_ID` after step 7, or retry advice on the cleanup step.
findings.resolution: fix-22: cleanup step 1 of ebs-t03 now says to wait one minute and run again if the volume is still being created. A wait step was refused by T102 (a try has 3 to 8 steps).

findings.section: ebs-t03 verify
findings.quote: "command": "aws ec2 describe-volumes --filters Name=tag:task,Values=ebs-t03 --query \"Volumes[].VolumeId\"", "expect": "An empty list. ... Then run the describe-snapshots command of \"Still costs money if left\": it must also return an empty list."
findings.type: technical: verify step does not prove the cleanup
findings.evidence: Rule: RULINGS hard rule 9 (a verify step on every Try). The verify command checks only volumes. The snapshot, the one resource that keeps billing at $0.05 per GB-month (ebs-snapshot-standard-price), is checked only by a command that the reader must find in another section. Make the verify cover both, for example a second verify command `aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --filters Name=tag:task,Values=ebs-t03 --query "Snapshots[].SnapshotId"`.
findings.resolution: fix-22: the verify expect of ebs-t03 now holds the full describe-snapshots command with the task tag filter; the verify object takes one command, so the snapshot check stays in expect.

findings.section: FAQ quick-fire, FAQ 4
findings.quote: Can you stop paying for provisioned IOPS by detaching the volume? -- No. > "Yes, you will be billed for the IOPS provisioned when it is disconnected from an instance."
findings.type: claims: answer and quote point in opposite directions
findings.evidence: The short answer 'No.' is followed by a quote that starts with 'Yes'. The reader skims and trusts the first word she sees (READER.md: 'trusts the gist she gets from one glance'). Rephrase the question to match the FAQ's own question (for example 'Are you still billed for provisioned IOPS after you detach the volume? Yes.').
findings.resolution: fix-22: FAQ 4 asks 'Are you still billed for provisioned IOPS after you detach the volume?' with the answer 'Yes.'

findings.section: The instance and its EBS bandwidth can cap a fast volume
findings.quote: Why does the instance matter? Every I/O leaves it, and EBS is a [multi-tenant block storage service](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-faq-multi-tenant-rate-limiting) that uses [rate limiting](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-faq-multi-tenant-rate-limiting).
findings.type: claims: link text right, sentence says more
findings.evidence: ebs-faq-multi-tenant-rate-limiting: 'EBS is a multi-tenant block storage service. We employ rate limiting as a mechanism to avoid resource contention.' This is rate limiting on the EBS side; it does not explain why the instance type caps performance. The supporting facts are ebs-instance-performance-bounded-by-smaller and ebs-optimized-dedicated-bandwidth (dedicated bandwidth for EBS I/O per instance). Replace the reason.
findings.resolution: fix-22: reason now the instance's own link to EBS with dedicated bandwidth (ebs-optimized-dedicated-bandwidth); the multi-tenant rate-limiting link is gone.

findings.type: claims: condition dropped from a fact

findings.type: technical: condition dropped from a fact

findings.section: SSD volumes serve small random IO and HDD volumes serve large sequential reads
findings.quote: Why do small random reads fail on HDD? There, an I/O of [1 MiB or less counts as a 1 MiB I/O credit]
findings.type: claims: overstatement
findings.evidence: ebs-faq-hdd-not-for-random-small-io: a transactional workload with small, random IOs 'won't perform well on HDD-backed volumes'. They do not fail; they perform poorly. Use 'perform poorly'.
findings.resolution: fix-22: 'Why is HDD bad at small random reads?' plus the cause and effect of the 1 MiB credit.

findings.section: SSD volumes serve small random IO ... (Stop and answer)
findings.quote: A weekly job scans 10 TB of logs. Which is cheapest, st1 or sc1? -- sc1, at [the lowest cost per GB], because the job scans rarely.
findings.type: technical: oversimplified decision rule
findings.evidence: ebs-st1-vs-sc1-scan-choice: 'If you are optimizing for cost, your data is relatively infrequently accessed, and you don't need more than 250 MiB/s of scanning performance, then use sc1.' The answer leaves out the 250 MiB/s condition (ebs-sc1-max-throughput 'maximum of 250 MiB/s'), which decides between the two when a scan has a deadline. Add 'and it needs no more than 250 MiB/s'.
findings.resolution: fix-22: answer adds the sc1 maximum of 250 MiB/s and the st1 case with a maximum of 500 MiB/s.

findings.type: claims: unsupported claim

Link it, or limit the sentence to zone and Region (ebs-snapshot-regional-copy-before-sharing).

findings.quote: A restored database volume appears in seconds, but the first queries are slow. ... 3. **Or pay to skip the wait.**

'pay' for fast snapshot restore and for an initialization rate has no fact link, although both are billed features (the page has a 'Billing' subsection for the initialization rate). findings.section: Words that go together
findings.quote: | ephemeral (ih-FEM-er-ul) | ephemeral **storage** | Temporary: the data disappears when its host stops | persistent |
findings.type: technical: imprecise definition
findings.evidence: instance-store-data-persists-reboot-not-stop: 'the data does not persist if the instance is stopped, hibernated, or terminated'. The instance stops, not its host, and the data also disappears at hibernation, at termination and when the disk fails (instance-store-data-lost-when-disk-fails). Suggest: 'the data disappears when the instance stops or ends'.
findings.resolution: fix-22: 'the data disappears when the instance stops or ends'.

findings.section: ebs-t02 and ebs-t03 permissions
findings.quote: "kms:ReEncrypt"
findings.type: technical: permission name
findings.evidence: The EBS guide's user-permission list writes `kms:ReEncrypt` (docs/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption-requirements line 32), but the same guide's policy examples use "kms:ReEncrypt*" (docs/ebs/latest/userguide/share-kms-key line 47; share-volume line 137). A reader who copies `kms:ReEncrypt` into a policy gets an action that matches nothing. Write `kms:ReEncrypt*` (or ReEncryptFrom and ReEncryptTo).

findings.section: ebs-s01 sixty_second
findings.quote: If the instance dies, we attach the volume to a new one.
findings.type: technical: spoken answer omits a condition and the question asked
findings.evidence: ebs-volume-same-az-as-instance: 'The volume and instance must be in the same Availability Zone.' The new instance must be launched in the volume's zone; say so. The prompt also asks 'how long are we offline?', and no line answers it (the story target is RTO 8 hours, STARTUP.md line 94; a restored volume is slow at first, ebs-volume-initialization-from-snapshot).
findings.resolution: fix-22: ebs-s01 says the new instance is in the same zone (kp1 links ebs-volume-same-az-as-instance) and answers the time question as 'within hours' and 'a rebuild takes hours'; P109 refuses story numbers such as eight hours in speak scripts.
